rubrics.evidence: Final selection rules: “Choose independent venture building as the central learning mechanism regardless of which educational format you add.” Phases 2–5 require customer interviews, prototypes, paid pilots, an MVP and financial models.
rubrics.reason: Practical venture-building determines the roadmap and its deliverables. Another degree is explicitly deprioritized and reserved for a demonstrated ecosystem, technical-access or career-transition need.

rubrics.evidence: The baseline is a “12-month validation track at 6–8 hours per week.” Phase 4 requires that cohort work can coexist with the job; the overload rules state, “A demanding cohort program should replace, not supplement, most self-study.”
rubrics.reason: Work and family constraints materially shape scheduling, course selection, workload limits and alternative branches. Intensive accelerators and full-time degrees are conditional options requiring explicit career and family decisions.

rubrics.evidence: Phase 1 includes applied work and interviews during Months 1–2; Phase 2 requires 40–50 customer interviews during Months 2–4. Phase 3 calls for “the cheapest credible test,” including concierge services, deposits and paid pilots, followed by a Month 6 proceed/pivot/archive gate.
rubrics.reason: Discovery begins alongside a compact foundation rather than after extensive coursework. Low-cost behavioral tests and explicit staged decision gates determine whether further investment is justified.

rubrics.evidence: Phase 3 instructs: “Use the Business Model Canvas as a versioned hypothesis system. Update it only when evidence changes.” It requires conversion, payment, repeat-use, acquisition-cost and margin tracking; later phases require a 13-week cash forecast and financing scenarios.
rubrics.reason: Concrete frameworks and collected market evidence are applied directly to product, pricing, opportunity selection and financing decisions. Although in-depth case selections are limited, the roadmap consequentially emphasizes applied decision-making rather than abstract theory.

rubrics.evidence: Executive programs must offer specific practical benefits, and the report says, “Avoid expensive programs dominated by general strategy, marketing or leadership content you have already covered.” The degree branch calculates tuition, living costs, lost compensation, benefits and family disruption against protected venture-building time.
rubrics.reason: Cost, opportunity cost and incremental practical value drive the recommended low-cost baseline and conditional program upgrades. Prestige-oriented options are explicitly subordinated to venture outcomes, relevant access and demonstrated capability gaps.
